prompt_en: Autumn fashion in a complex, connected everyday moment. A reference-guided fashion subject, portrayed as a generated adult woman, is working at a small rooftop theatre rehearsal as an autumn gust lifts the loose corner of a painted canvas backdrop. Her visible face and hair cues follow the supplied image: the same softly tapered facial outline, rounded dark eyes, small straight nose and softly full lips, with a short black bob curving around the jaw and a light, wispy fringe crossing the forehead. Her individual presence comes through attentive concentration and a quiet ease in the cold air. She is wearing autumn layers: an open cropped cocoa-and-charcoal tweed jacket over a wine-red cropped cardigan and a fine cream rib-knit roll-neck, with a knee-length checked wool skirt in deep box pleats and dark chocolate leather knee boots. The cream knit collar rises above both outer necklines, and its narrow cuffs emerge beyond the tweed sleeves. Her wine-red cropped cardigan closes in a slim column of small buttons, with its lower edge meeting the top of her checked skirt waistband. The open tweed jacket stops slightly higher, leaving the cardigan's buttoned hem and the skirt's first opening pleat readable together. The skirt checks turn with the box folds, and soft creases at the boot ankles register her planted weight. On her tweed jacket, the garment's fabric texture or sheen is distinguishable in tiny raised cocoa-and-charcoal speckles. The sleeve folds originate at a seam joint or pulling contact, gathering from her right elbow seam. Their fold direction agrees with the body's action or pose as the jacket sleeve bends with her forearm toward the ring. Those folds preserve the garment silhouette and closure, leaving the open front edges and cuff outline continuous. These tactile layers remain the strongest visual rhythm after her face and hands. Both boots are planted on dry wooden boards, her left foot half a step forward and knees softly bent, with her shoulders balanced over her feet. A brass ring fixed to a waist-high backstage rail sits on her right side, clear of the jacket front. Her right hand grips the doubled canvas seam just beyond the ring and draws the corner through it; her left hand holds the folded edge against the near side of the ring, keeping the loop from slipping back. Each forearm leads visibly from its own sleeve to its hand. The gathered corner now hangs as a compact vertical tail beneath the ring, while the free upper canvas still bows in the wind. Its painted blue arch is kinked by the pulled fold, making the change in tension visible. Her gaze rests on the attachment, her lips gently parted as the next knot waits to be made. A chalk stage mark and two folded rehearsal chairs situate this brief repair within the rehearsal space. Photograph the moment from a front three-quarter position at her waist height, in a vertical 4:5 full-length environmental frame with her face, both hands, the ring, skirt folds and boots visible together. Place the moving canvas toward the right edge and leave breathing space around the attachment. Cool late-afternoon skylight reveals the tweed and wool surfaces; a warm rehearsal lamp by the open theatre door gives a small amber edge to her cheek and knit collar. Keep natural skin texture, believable fabric weight and moderate depth of field, with the subject and contact plane crisp and the distant roof parapet softly receding.
